system_prompt_style.note: Jinja2 templates rendered with INSTRUCTION and tool list.

context_compaction.evidence_quote: we conducted a preliminary experiment (the right of Figure 4) by introducing a summarization agent at each step, designed to compress the raw outputs of the MCP servers
context_compaction.note: Optional summarization agent; default ReAct sends full history.

observation_format.note: Tool results returned as text (often JSON strings) into the conversation.

tool_call_format.note: Default ReAct agent emits JSON in text; FunctionCallAgent 'Uses LLM native tool calling APIs'.

tool_count.note: Tool count depends on the MCP servers named in each task (133 tools across 11 servers overall); no fixed default count.

edit_primitive.evidence_quote: Tavailable = S i∈ITi is the set of tools accessible for the task
edit_primitive.note: No harness-side edit primitive; editing only via MCP server tools (e.g., GitHub).

tool_schema_source.evidence_quote: Each server is configured with its authentic API endpoints, authentication mechanisms, and tool specifications
tool_schema_source.note: Schemas come from MCP servers; rendered into a tools prompt.

protocol_standardization.evidence_quote: MCP standardizes how an agent calls tools, and a large ecosystem of MCP servers already exists.

loop_primitives.evidence_quote: we adopt the most popular framework, ReAct [29]. The LLMs first generate a thought based on the observation, and then generate the next action based on that thought.
loop_primitives.note: Default ReAct; 'ReAct with Exploration' variant adds an exploration phase; workflows (Chain, Router, Orchestrator) are config-reachable.

planning_granularity.evidence_quote: The LLMs first generate a thought based on the observation, and then generate the next action based on that thought.
planning_granularity.note: No stored plan object in the default ReAct agent.

BenchmarkRunner

state_persistence.note: Traces are collected but no documented resume path.

self_verification.evidence_quote: we choose to follow the execution-based paradigm to evaluate the completion of tasks
self_verification.note: Execution-based evaluators score after the run; they are benchmark scoring, not feedback to the agent. ReflectionAgent (self_critique) is config-reachable.

retry_policy.note: One attempt per task; no retry loop described.

rollback.evidence_quote: The AI agent will perform real operations on GitHub repositories, which could potentially modify or damage your personal repositories.
rollback.note: Real side effects on live services; no rollback mechanism.

termination_condition.note: max_iterations cap plus the agent returning a final answer.

cost_controls.note: Iteration cap only; no token/cost budget or caching documented. MCP+ token-reduction wrapper is a separate add-on.

execution_isolation.note: MCP servers launched as local stdio processes (Docker used for some servers); agent actions hit live external services.

filesystem_access.evidence_quote: The 3D design benchmarks will execute Blender commands that may modify or create files on your system.

network_policy.evidence_quote: our framework seamlessly integrates with diverse MCP servers representing real-world tools and services. Each server is configured with its authentic API endpoints

permission_model.evidence_quote: Grant minimal necessary permissions for each service integration
permission_model.note: Authorisation is left to external API key scopes; no in-harness per-action gate.
